```{python}
# | label: setup
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib as mpl
import seaborn as sns

# DejaVu Sans is matplotlib's default and ships full Cyrillic coverage, so
# any Russian labels left on the figures render correctly inside the PDF.
mpl.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",
    "figure.dpi": 150,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.25,
    "axes.titlesize": 12,
    "axes.titleweight": "bold",
})
sns.set_palette("colorblind")

ACCENT = "#2b6cb0"      # useful / neutral primary
RISK = "#c05621"        # risk factors

DATA = Path("../data/raw/objects_arkhangelsk_2026-06-28_enriched.csv")
df = pd.read_csv(DATA, sep=";", encoding="utf-8-sig", low_memory=False)

# --- English labels for the report (source data is in Russian) ------------
CATEGORY_EN = {
    "Магазины": "Shops",
    "Организации": "Organizations",
    "Медицинские организации": "Medical organizations",
    "Услуги": "Services",
    "Общепит": "Catering",
    "Образование": "Education",
    "Спортивные объекты": "Sport facilities",
    "Государственные организации": "Government organizations",
    "фастфуд": "Fast food",
    "Финансовые организации": "Financial organizations",
    "Почта и связь": "Post & communications",
    "Авто": "Auto",
    "Культура": "Culture",
    "Досуг и спорт": "Leisure & sport",
    "Точки продажи табака": "Tobacco outlets",
    "Гостиницы и туризм": "Hotels & tourism",
}
DISTRICT_EN = {
    "Октябрьский округ": "Oktyabrsky",
    "Округ Майская горка": "Mayskaya Gorka",
    "Соломбальский округ": "Solombalsky",
    "Округ Варавино-Фактория": "Varavino-Faktoriya",
    "Северный округ": "Severny",
    "Исакогорский и Цигломенский округа": "Isakogorsky & Tsiglomensky",
    "Ломоносовский округ": "Lomonosovsky",
    "Маймаксанский округ": "Maymaksansky",
}
VERIF_EN = {
    "only_osm": "OSM only",
    "only_2gis": "2GIS only",
    "confirmed_by_2gis_and_osm": "OSM + 2GIS (confirmed)",
}

df["category_en"] = df["category_orig"].map(CATEGORY_EN).fillna(df["category_orig"])
df["district_en"] = df["district_orig"].map(DISTRICT_EN).fillna(df["district_orig"])
df["verif_en"] = df["verification_status"].map(VERIF_EN).fillna(df["verification_status"])

n_obj = len(df)
n_cat = df["category_orig"].nunique()
n_type = df["type_orig"].nunique()
n_dist = df["district_orig"].nunique()


def barh(series, title, xlabel, color=ACCENT, fmt_pct=False, figsize=(7.2, 4.4)):
    """Horizontal bar chart, largest on top, with value labels."""
    s = series.sort_values(ascending=True)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    ax.barh(s.index, s.values, color=color)
    total = s.sum()
    for y, v in enumerate(s.values):
        lbl = f"{v:,} ({v/total*100:.0f}%)" if fmt_pct else f"{v:,}"
        ax.text(v, y, " " + lbl, va="center", ha="left", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.margins(x=0.14)
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

# Introduction

This report is the **initial exploratory data analysis (EDA)** of the current
stage of the Northern State Medical University infrastructure project. The
research question — inherited from the 2022 stage (see
[`../docs/report_arkhangelsk_2022.md`](../docs/report_arkhangelsk_2022.md)) — is
**how health-relevant urban infrastructure and health risk factors are
distributed across the districts (*okrugs*) of Arkhangelsk**.

The data is the enriched, cross-checked export produced by the *ИнфраструктураРФ*
program (see [`../docs/infrastructure_rf.md`](../docs/infrastructure_rf.md)) for
Arkhangelsk, dated **2026-06-28**. Each object was collected from open sources
(OpenStreetMap, 2GIS, and others) and passed through deduplication, verification,
and address backfilling.

```{python}
# | label: overview-table
overview = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "Metric": [
            "Objects (rows)",
            "Categories",
            "Object types",
            "Districts (okrugs)",
            "City",
            "Coordinate coverage",
            "Address coverage",
        ],
        "Value": [
            f"{n_obj:,}",
            f"{n_cat}",
            f"{n_type}",
            f"{n_dist}",
            "Arkhangelsk",
            f"{df['latitude'].notna().mean()*100:.0f}%",
            f"{df['adress_orig'].notna().mean()*100:.1f}%",
        ],
    }
)
overview.style.hide(axis="index")
```

# Data quality and source verification

Every object carries provenance and verification metadata. Confidence is higher
when an object is confirmed by more than one source.

```{python}
# | label: fig-verification
# | fig-cap: "Objects by verification status (data-source confidence)."
vc = df["verif_en"].value_counts()
barh(vc, "Verification status", "Number of objects", fmt_pct=True, figsize=(7.2, 2.9))
```

```{python}
# | label: verif-note
n_multi = int((df["provider_count"] >= 2).sum())
osm_only = int((df["verification_status"] == "only_osm").sum())
```

Only **`{python} f"{n_multi:,}"`** objects (`{python} f"{n_multi/n_obj*100:.1f}"`%)
are confirmed by both OpenStreetMap and 2GIS; the remaining objects come from a
single source, and **`{python} f"{osm_only/n_obj*100:.0f}"`%** rely on
OpenStreetMap alone. Analyses of absolute counts should therefore be read as
*lower bounds* — coverage depends heavily on OSM completeness, consistent with
the 2022 finding that ~64% of objects were found in OSM.

## Field completeness

```{python}
# | label: fig-completeness
# | fig-cap: "Share of objects with each attribute populated."
fields = {
    "Address": "adress_orig",
    "Opening hours": "opening_hours_orig",
    "Phone": "phone_orig",
    "Website": "website_orig",
    "Opening date": "opening_date_orig",
}
cov = pd.Series({k: df[v].notna().mean() * 100 for k, v in fields.items()})
cov = cov.sort_values()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.0))
ax.barh(cov.index, cov.values, color=ACCENT)
for y, v in enumerate(cov.values):
    ax.text(v, y, f" {v:.0f}%", va="center", fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlim(0, 100)
ax.set_xlabel("% of objects populated")
ax.set_title("Attribute completeness")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Addresses and coordinates are nearly complete, so **spatial analysis is
reliable**. Contact details are partial, and *opening date* is essentially
absent (<1%) and should be dropped from downstream analysis.

# Category composition

```{python}
# | label: fig-categories
# | fig-cap: "Objects by category (English labels; source categories are in Russian)."
cat = df["category_en"].value_counts()
barh(cat, "Objects by category", "Number of objects", fmt_pct=True, figsize=(7.2, 5.2))
```

The export is a **general city inventory**, not only health objects: retail
(*Shops*), generic *Organizations*, *Services*, and *Catering* dominate.
Health-relevant categories — *Medical organizations*, *Sport facilities* — and
explicit risk categories (*Fast food*, *Tobacco outlets*) are present but are a
minority of the raw export, which motivates the targeted classification in
Section 6.

# Spatial and district distribution

All objects are geocoded within the Arkhangelsk bounding box
(lat 64.41–64.71, lon 40.25–40.78).

```{python}
# | label: fig-map
# | fig-cap: "Spatial distribution of objects, coloured by district (okrug)."
top_d = df["district_en"].value_counts().index.tolist()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 6.0))
palette = sns.color_palette("colorblind", len(top_d))
for color, d in zip(palette, top_d):
    sub = df[df["district_en"] == d]
    ax.scatter(sub["longitude"], sub["latitude"], s=6, alpha=0.5,
               color=color, label=f"{d} ({len(sub):,})")
ax.set_xlabel("Longitude")
ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")
ax.set_title("Objects by district")
ax.set_aspect(1 / np.cos(np.deg2rad(64.55)))  # approx. metric aspect at this latitude
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=7, markerscale=2, framealpha=0.9)
ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: fig-districts
# | fig-cap: "Objects per district (okrug)."
dist = df["district_en"].value_counts()
barh(dist, "Objects by district", "Number of objects", fmt_pct=True, figsize=(7.2, 3.8))
```

```{python}
# | label: dist-note
okt = df["district_en"].value_counts()
okt_share = okt.iloc[0] / n_obj * 100
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Data-quality caveat: district assignment is skewed

**`{python} f"{okt_share:.0f}"`% of all objects are assigned to a single okrug
(Oktyabrsky).** This is inconsistent with the geography of Arkhangelsk and with
the 2022 stage, where Oktyabrsky, Lomonosovsky, and Mayskaya Gorka held
comparable counts. Here *Lomonosovsky* has only 33 objects and *Maymaksansky*
only 5. The most likely cause is an issue in the automatic okrug-assignment step
of the export (e.g., a default/fallback okrug). **District-level rates below
should be treated as provisional and the assignment logic re-validated before
any substantive spatial conclusions.**
:::

## Category mix by district

```{python}
# | label: fig-heatmap
# | fig-cap: "Category share within each district (column-normalised, %)."
top_cats = df["category_en"].value_counts().head(10).index
top_dists = df["district_en"].value_counts().head(6).index
ct = pd.crosstab(df["category_en"], df["district_en"])
ct = ct.loc[ct.index.isin(top_cats), ct.columns.isin(top_dists)]
ct = ct.loc[top_cats.intersection(ct.index), top_dists.intersection(ct.columns)]
ct_pct = ct.div(ct.sum(axis=0), axis=1) * 100
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 5.0))
sns.heatmap(ct_pct, annot=True, fmt=".0f", cmap="Blues", cbar_kws={"label": "% of district"},
            linewidths=0.5, linecolor="white", ax=ax)
ax.set_xlabel("")
ax.set_ylabel("")
ax.set_title("Category share within district (%)")
plt.xticks(rotation=30, ha="right")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Health infrastructure vs. risk factors

Following the project's *"Health + risks"* framing, objects are classified with a
transparent keyword rule over `category_orig` and `type_orig`. The rule is a
first-pass heuristic for EDA, not a validated instrument.

```{python}
# | label: classify
cat = df["category_orig"].fillna("")
typ = df["type_orig"].fillna("")
name = df["name_orig"].fillna("")
blob = (cat + " | " + typ + " | " + name).str.lower()

def has(s, *words):
    return s.apply(lambda x: any(w in x for w in words))

health = {
    "Medical": (cat == "Медицинские организации") | has(typ.str.lower(), "аптека", "поликлин", "больниц", "стоматолог", "врач", "диагност", "лаборатор"),
    "Sport": (cat == "Спортивные объекты") | has(blob, "спорт", "фитнес", "бассейн", "стадион"),
}
risk = {
    "Fast food": (cat == "фастфуд") | has(typ.str.lower(), "фастфуд"),
    "Alcohol": has(typ.str.lower(), "алкогол") | has(blob, "алкомаркет", "винный магазин"),
    "Tobacco": (cat == "Точки продажи табака") | has(blob, "табак", "вейп", "сигарет"),
    "Bars": has(typ.str.lower(), "бар") & ~has(typ.str.lower(), "барбер"),
    "Hookah / nightlife": has(blob, "кальян", "ночной клуб", "лаунж"),
}

health_mask = np.logical_or.reduce(list(health.values()))
risk_mask = np.logical_or.reduce(list(risk.values()))

hr = pd.DataFrame({
    "Group": ["Health-supporting"] * len(health) + ["Risk factor"] * len(risk),
    "Subgroup": list(health.keys()) + list(risk.keys()),
    "Objects": [int(m.sum()) for m in health.values()] + [int(m.sum()) for m in risk.values()],
})
```

```{python}
# | label: fig-healthrisk
# | fig-cap: "Health-supporting infrastructure vs. risk factors (heuristic classification)."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.2))
colors = [ACCENT if g == "Health-supporting" else RISK for g in hr["Group"]]
order = hr.sort_values("Objects")
ax.barh(order["Subgroup"], order["Objects"],
        color=[ACCENT if g == "Health-supporting" else RISK for g in order["Group"]])
for y, v in enumerate(order["Objects"]):
    ax.text(v, y, f" {v:,}", va="center", fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("Number of objects")
ax.set_title("Health-supporting (blue) vs. risk factors (orange)")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.margins(x=0.12)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

n_health = int(health_mask.sum())
n_risk = int(risk_mask.sum())
```

Under this heuristic the export contains **`{python} f"{n_health:,}"`
health-supporting** objects and **`{python} f"{n_risk:,}"` risk-factor** objects.
A useful summary indicator for later stages is the **health-to-risk ratio** per
district, which the next stage can compute once the district-assignment issue
(Section 5) is resolved.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-healthrisk-district
# | tbl-cap: "Health-supporting vs. risk objects by district (provisional — see Section 5 caveat)."
tmp = df.copy()
tmp["is_health"] = health_mask
tmp["is_risk"] = risk_mask
g = tmp.groupby("district_en").agg(
    Objects=("name_orig", "size"),
    Health=("is_health", "sum"),
    Risk=("is_risk", "sum"),
)
g["Health:Risk"] = (g["Health"] / g["Risk"].replace(0, np.nan)).round(2)
g = g.sort_values("Objects", ascending=False)
(g.reset_index()
  .rename(columns={"district_en": "District"})
  .style.hide(axis="index")
  .format({"Health:Risk": "{:.2f}"}, na_rep="—"))
```

# Key findings

1. **Scale & scope.** The 2026 export covers **`{python} f"{n_obj:,}"` objects**
   across **`{python} f"{n_cat}"` categories** and **`{python} f"{n_type}"`
   types** — a general city inventory, far larger than the 2,528-object,
   three-okrug 2022 dataset.
2. **Source confidence is thin.** Only
   **`{python} f"{n_multi/n_obj*100:.1f}"`%** of objects are multi-source
   confirmed; ~**`{python} f"{osm_only/n_obj*100:.0f}"`%** are OSM-only. Counts
   are lower bounds.
3. **Geometry is solid, attributes are partial.** Coordinates and addresses are
   near-complete (good for spatial work); phone/website are partial; *opening
   date* is unusable (<1%).
4. **District assignment is broken.** ~**`{python} f"{okt_share:.0f}"`%** of
   objects fall into one okrug — this must be fixed before any district-level
   health-accessibility conclusions.
5. **Health vs. risk is measurable.** A transparent heuristic already separates
   health-supporting infrastructure from risk factors, giving the next stage a
   concrete **health-to-risk** indicator to map across the city.

## Recommended next steps

- Re-validate the okrug-assignment step of the export (highest priority).
- Formalise the health / risk-factor taxonomy (replace the EDA heuristic with a
  reviewed keyword/category mapping, aligned with the 2022 categories).
- Enrich source confidence by pulling additional providers (Yandex, 2GIS,
  administrative data) as in the 2022 methodology.
- Once districts are fixed, compute per-district, per-capita accessibility and
  the health-to-risk ratio as the core project output.

# Appendix: dataset dictionary {.appendix}

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `verification_status` | Source confirmation tier (`only_osm`, `only_2gis`, `confirmed_by_2gis_and_osm`) |
| `providers` / `provider_count` | Which sources found the object / how many |
| `verification_comment` | Free-text verification note |
| `filled_fields` / `missing_fields` | Attributes present / absent after enrichment |
| `website_check_status` | Result of website reachability check |
| `matched_source_ids` | Source object IDs matched during dedup |
| `match_distance_meters` / `match_name_similarity` | Cross-source match geometry / name score |
| `category_orig` / `type_orig` | Category and fine-grained type (Russian) |
| `name_orig` | Object name |
| `city_orig` / `district_orig` / `adress_orig` | Location text fields |
| `latitude` / `longitude` | Coordinates (WGS84) |
| `website_orig` / `phone_orig` / `opening_hours_orig` / `opening_date_orig` | Contact & schedule |
| `enrichment_comment` | Free-text enrichment note |
